# Outward smoothing without H: actual attainment, singleton sources, and fixed-menu stress

The H buffer can be removed from the outward uniform smoothing problem.
At every fixed sufficiently small h>0 the actual cap first-order equations
force unique deepest marks and distinct source parities. Frozen selected
normals supply an exact finite cover under body variation, hence one
simultaneous physical-field separator. Arbitrary independent signed normal
variations do NOT inherit the H unique-contact envelope; they are neither
used nor needed below.

Dependencies are the original compact minimal-bad-base class and actual
convex physical body fields already proved in the H response companion,
and the C1/clipping estimates in
`candidate 0fa64553cd01d7ae`.
The claims are conditional on that original minimal-bad framework, not a
new unconditional compactness theorem for all convex families.

## 1. Unbuffered outward smoothing and its actual minimum

Let P be the fixed finite complete base, K_z positive compatible fibers,
M=sum_z |K_z|, Sigma their pooled within-fiber covariance, and
Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u). For u!=0 put

    Q_h(K;N,c)=integral Psi((N.w-c)/(h Gamma(u))) dmu,
    Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)),  N=(a,u).

At an actual mark Y use c=N.Y. Pure-base caps remain their ordinary closed
caps. Let beta_h be maximal raw mixed depth divided by M. Fubini gives

    Q_h(N,N.Y)=(1/h) integral_0^h mu{N.w>=N.Y-s Gamma(u)} ds,
    beta_h>=beta_0.                                    (1)

On the original compact normalized bad-sublevel class A,

    0<=beta_h-beta_0<=C h,                             (2)

uniformly in marks and ALL base tilts. The proof is the uniform fiber slab
bound, which does not depend on a. The same symmetric-difference/slab
argument proves simultaneous body/mark continuity. For a fixed strict bad
trial and sufficiently small h, its value remains below the chosen bad
threshold. By (1), every minimizing sequence is in the original bad
sublevel and admits the original affine normalization. Thus an ACTUAL
unrestricted body minimum exists for each sufficiently small fixed h.

On A an ordinary maximal-depth lower bound q0>0 is fixed. Ordinary own-
boundary depth is0 and its mark dependence is uniformly Lipschitz. By
(2), every h-deepest mark has a uniform own inball once Ch<q0/4. All own
width-h strips through such a mark therefore have uniform proper coarea.
The pure-base reserve is unchanged:

    baseDepth(p)-Q_h >= V_p/2-C h >= v0/4.

Here Q_h is the maximal raw depth, M=1 in the normalized class. Thus no
active pure-base cap occurs. Exact finite base-tilt clipping survives the
kernel's saturation outside [-1,0]. Normalize Gamma(u)=1. Active caps
have bounded actual clipped representatives, their family is compact,
and each is attained with

    S=integral psi(q)/h, m=integral w psi(q)/h,
    A=integral q psi(q), q=(N.w-N.Y)/h,
    S_min<=S<=S_max, -hS<=A<=0.                        (3)

All constants in this paragraph are uniform for sufficiently small h.
The kernel is not pointwise C1, but its cap integral is C1: each kink plane
has zero d-volume in every positive fiber, and dominated differentiation
and parameter continuity apply.

## 2. Full cap stationarity supplies strict singleton sources

At an attained minimizing cap the derivative in every full normal
direction vanishes. Differentiating the ACTUAL through-mark functional,
including Gamma(u), yields

    m_base/S=p,
    m_cont/S=y+(A/S) grad Gamma(u).

Equivalently, with m_eff=m-A(0,grad Gamma(u)),

    m_eff/S=Y.                                        (4)

These equations hold cap by cap, before any body separator is selected.

For each fixed nonvertical N the tail has strictly negative threshold
derivative -S at an active threshold. Hence its maximal-depth Q quantile
c_Q(N) is unique, and the actual Q-depth superlevel is described by

    N.Y<=c_Q(N)

together with the pure-base constraints. In particular the ambient
superlevel is convex. Suppose distinct deepest marks Y_i have a convex
combination Y=sum theta_i Y_i whose base is integer, with all theta_i>0.
Compatibility makes Y feasible and the linear inequalities make it
deepest. An attained active cap at Y has

    c_Q=N.Y=sum theta_i N.Y_i<=c_Q.

Thus this SAME cap is active at every Y_i. Its cap data N,c,S,m,A are the
same. Equation (4) forces every Y_i=m_eff/S, a contradiction.

Consequences at each fixed h>0:

* There is a unique deepest mark at each deepest base.
* No nontrivial convex combination of distinct deepest bases is integer.
* Deepest bases are the vertices of an empty lattice polytope and have
  distinct parity, so their number is at most k(P)<=2^n.

This strictness uses h>0 and active differentiability. It is not asserted
for h=0, and limits of the positive-width source menu may omit new deepest
marks that appear at h=0.

## 3. Actual finite menus and an exact frozen-normal cover

At each interior deepest mark Y_i=(p_i,y_i), compact active-cap minimization
and Caratheodory give at most d+1 selected actual active caps and positive
rho_ij of sum1 such that

    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0, Gamma(u_ij)=1,
    c_ij=N_ij.Y_i, Q_h(N_ij,c_ij)=Q.                   (5)

For the mark derivative one first balances S_ij u_ij, then absorbs the
positive S_ij into the weights, which gives precisely (5).

Fix these normals during any actual convex physical body deformation
K(t). The width still follows Gamma_t(u_j). Let c_ij(t,q) be the exact
nearby threshold having raw smoothed mass q. It is defined by the implicit
function theorem because S_ij>0. Solve the scalar equation

    sum_j rho_ij c_ij(t,q_i(t))
                       =sum_j rho_ij a_ij.p_i.        (6)

At t=0 it holds with q_i(0)=Q. Its q derivative is
-B_i, B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij>0, so q_i(t) is well-defined.

Equation (6) covers the ENTIRE current source fiber at p_i. Indeed if all
selected through-mark caps at w=(p_i,x) had mass greater than q_i(t), then
N_ij.w<c_ij(t,q_i(t)) for every j. Their positive weighted sum contradicts
(5)--(6). Thus some selected cap has mass at most q_i(t). This argument
allows all equality points and does not require any unique affine contact.
The finite optimized-depth gaps on all other bases persist by continuity.
Therefore simultaneous strict descent of every q_i(t)/M(t) gives actual
global objective descent.

The old contact function sum rho(N.w-c) is identically zero on the own
fiber. With independent normal velocities its contact derivative would
be min_(x in K_pi) sum rho dot u.x plus base terms, not evaluation at y_i.
No such linearization is claimed. Frozen normals suffice for (6) and the
physical separator. Balanced normal velocities could also be admitted,
but are unnecessary here.

## 4. Exact body response and one simultaneous separator

Let v be inward normal speed, D=sum_z integral_boundary v_z, and

    J_ij=sum_z integral_boundary [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2 v_z,
    B_ij(v)=integral_boundary Psi(q_ij) v.

Holding the cap normal fixed gives the exact covariance response

    dot Gamma_ij=(D-J_ij)/(2M).

If its threshold velocity is r_ij, its captured-volume loss is

    L_ij=B_ij(v)+S_ij r_ij+A_ij(D-J_ij)/(2M).          (7)

Differentiate (6): sum rho r=0. Equalizing the cap losses consequently
gives the exact group loss

    l_i=[sum_j (rho_ij/S_ij)
                     (B_ij+A_ij(D-J_ij)/(2M))]/B_i.  (8)

This is linear on the actual addable cone of convex physical fields.
At an actual body minimum, no field gives l_i-beta_h D>0 for every group.
For each finite field list, finite-dimensional separation gives
lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1. The compact lambda simplex and the finite-
intersection property then give ONE lambda valid for every actual convex
physical field simultaneously. This uses exactly the old finite-list
separation argument; it requires no signed cap-normal variables.

Put

    omega_ij=lambda_i rho_ij/(B_i S_ij), sum omega_ij=1,
    W=sum omega_ij Psi(q_ij), Abar=sum omega_ij A_ij<=0.

For every realized normal-dependent convex physical field Phi,

    integral_boundary Xi_h Phi <=0,                  (9)

where the exact density is

    Xi_h=W-beta_h
        +(1/(2M)) sum_ij omega_ij(-A_ij)
                                  [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
        +Abar/(2M).                                  (10)

The positive side is W plus the nonnegative width-covariance term. Its
constant comparison density is beta_h-Abar/(2M). The source-energy,
source-volume and epsilon covariance terms have all disappeared. The
full normal moment identities (4) still hold individually, independently
of lambda or the restriction to frozen normals.

## 5. Width scale and zero-width scope

On the compact class, 0<=-Abar<=hS_max, so (10) differs uniformly by O(h)
from W-beta_h. This does not make its width-scale information negligible
if one divides by h. Optional logarithmic width minimization has the exact
scalar coefficient Abar: for s=dot(log h), captured-volume loss includes
A_ij s. Thus an attained interior minimum of beta_h-tau log h satisfies

    -Abar=M tau.                                     (11)

Existence and interior scale selection can be obtained by the same trial
and compactness argument as for epsilon, once one uses the uniform linear
gap c h<=beta_h-beta_0<=C h. For the lower bound, at an ordinary deepest
mark each nonvertical outward cap gains a uniform own-ball strip of mean
width h Gamma/2, whereas pure-base caps retain the fixed reserve. The
uniform source ball and covariance floor give c>0. No energy buffer is
involved.

One may instead keep fixed h throughout; (9)--(10) do not require scale
selection. As h decreases to0, actual body minima have compact subsequences
and all retained cap masses converge to the ordinary maximal depth. The
limiting selected menu need not cover newly appearing deepest bases.
The boundary capture/section selectors and endpoint transition records
must be extracted from the same actual sequence as before. There is no
claim that the unbuffered stress alone proves Gamma_d/k(P).
